one_liner: A stateless LangChain chat assistant for Harbor Hotels (Lisbon, Porto, Bergen) that checks room availability and rates and books rooms, over an OpenAI-chat-completions HTTP endpoint.
system_prompt_excerpt:
SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are the reservations assistant for Harbor Hotels, a small hotel group with "
    "properties in Lisbon, Porto and Bergen. You help guests check availability and book "
    "rooms. Rules: never invent a rate or availability, always call check_availability "
    "before quoting a price; only call book_room after the guest has confirmed the city, "
    "room type, number of nights and the name for the booking; amounts are in euros; if the "
    "guest asks for anything other than hotel bookings (flights, tours, restaurants), say "
    "that you can only help with Harbor Hotels bookings."
)
hard_constraints: never invent a rate or availability
always call check_availability before quoting a price
only call book_room after the guest has confirmed the city, room type, number of nights and the name for the booking
if the guest asks for anything other than hotel bookings (flights, tours, restaurants), say that you can only help with Harbor Hotels bookings

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Check a Harbor Hotels room and return its nightly rate in euros. city is lisbon, porto or bergen. room_type is standard, harbor_view or suite. nights is a whole number from 1 to 14.
tools.refuses: Returned as an ordinary string, not an error, always starting 'unavailable: '. Checks run in this order: (1) city (stripped, case-insensitive) not in lisbon/porto/bergen -> 'unavailable: no Harbor Hotels property in {city}; cities are lisbon, porto, bergen'; (2) room_type (stripped, case-insensitive) not standard/harbor_view/suite -> 'unavailable: unknown room type {room_type}; types are standard, harbor_view, suite'; (3) nights not an int or outside 1..14 -> 'unavailable: nights must be a whole number from 1 to 14'; (4) the (porto, harbor_view) combination is permanently sold out -> 'unavailable: the harbor_view room in {city} is sold out'. Note: the sold-out check applies regardless of nights.
tools.effects: Read-only. Looks up the rate in the in-memory RATES table and returns 'available: {rate} EUR per night, {rate*nights} EUR for {nights} night(s)'. Changes nothing.

tools.name: book_room
tools.description: Book a room once the guest has confirmed city, room type, nights and name. Returns the booking code.
tools.refuses: Returned as an ordinary string, always starting 'not booked: '. Same validation and order as check_availability (city, room type, nights 1..14, sold-out porto/harbor_view), with the prefix 'not booked: ' instead of 'unavailable: '; then, only after those pass, an empty or whitespace-only guest_name -> 'not booked: a guest name is required'. So an invalid room with a blank name reports the room error first. The tool itself does not require check_availability to have been called first; that sequencing is only a prompt rule.
tools.effects: Creates a booking in the process-global in-memory BOOKINGS dict under code 'HH-{len(BOOKINGS)+1001}' (first is HH-1001, then HH-1002, ...), storing city and room_type (stripped, lowercased), nights, guest_name (stripped) and total_eur = rate*nights. Returns 'booked: code {code}, {total} EUR total for {nights} night(s)'. Bookings are shared across all conversations and persist until the process exits; no tool reads, changes or cancels them.

RATES.value: dict room_type (standard|harbor_view|suite) -> nightly rate in EUR (int)

dependencies.name: hotel_world
dependencies.what: Module-level in-memory dicts in agent.py: RATES (per-city, per-room nightly EUR rate), SOLD_OUT set, and BOOKINGS dict (starts empty, filled by book_room). No external database.

runtime_dependencies.name: model_provider
runtime_dependencies.what: LLM that drives the conversation and tool calls. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY is required (Anthropic wins if its key is set, unless HARBOR_PROVIDER says otherwise). OPENAI_BASE_URL/OPENAI_API_BASE optionally route OpenAI calls through a gateway.
runtime_dependencies.engine: anthropic or openai (via langchain_anthropic ChatAnthropic / langchain_openai ChatOpenAI)

runtime_dependencies.name: trace_export
runtime_dependencies.what: Optional trace export, started only when FI_BASE_URL is set or HARBOR_TRACING=on; off otherwise. The agent never reads FI_API_KEY/FI_SECRET_KEY.

tool_entrypoints.notes: A langchain_core @tool StructuredTool; call with .invoke({'city':..,'room_type':..,'nights':..}). Importing agent imports fi_instrumentation, traceai_langchain and langchain_core (installed from requirements.txt) but starts neither tracing nor the server (guarded by __main__). Fully local, no dependency endpoint.
A langchain_core @tool StructuredTool; call with .invoke({...}). Mutates module-global agent.BOOKINGS under a lock. Fully local, no dependency endpoint.

refusal_signature: Tools return plain strings and never raise for business refusals: check_availability returns a string beginning 'unavailable: ', book_room returns a string beginning 'not booked: '. Success strings begin 'available: ' and 'booked: '. Separately, the agent loop returns 'Sorry, I could not finish that request. Please try again.' after 6 model/tool steps, and an unknown tool name yields 'error: unknown tool {name}'.

data_store.configured_by: hardcoded module-level dicts in agent.py; no connection to configure
data_store.loaded_by: module import of agent.py (RATES, SOLD_OUT, BOOKINGS)

real_use_cases: Check whether a Harbor Hotels room (city, room type, nights) is available and quote its nightly rate and total in euros.
Book a room for a named guest once city, room type, nights and name are confirmed, returning a booking code.
Explain unavailability: unknown city or room type, nights outside 1-14, or the sold-out Porto harbor_view room.
Decline requests that are not Harbor Hotels bookings (flights, tours, restaurants).
caller_identity: The agent never identifies the caller. It is stateless: the caller sends the whole conversation (user/assistant messages) on every POST; system and tool messages sent by the caller are ignored. Nothing is loaded before a tool runs.
notes: Single-file agent (agent.py), one agent, one runtime (HTTP chat). There is NO Dockerfile, Compose file or Procfile in the repo (README says the harness runs 'python agent.py'); deployment is native Python startup, consistent with the available execution capabilities, so nothing from a Dockerfile is needed. README says venv python3.12; requirements.txt comments mention 3.11/3.13 installs; pins have not been re-resolved. Model: default is claude-sonnet-5-5 (Anthropic, written on line 48) when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else gpt-4o-mini; HARBOR_MODEL overrides; the HTTP response's 'model' field just echoes it and the request's model field is ignored. Tools execute inside the agent's loop (max 6 model steps per turn); the HTTP response only carries final assistant text and does not expose completed tool calls, so tool-call evidence is only available through traces (FI_BASE_URL/HARBOR_TRACING=on) — no completed_tools mapping is declared. Endpoints: GET /health -> {status: ok}; POST /v1/chat/completions needs 'messages' list (else 400 messages_required); internal failures return 500 {error:{type:<ExceptionClass>}}; other paths 404. If the messages contain no user message, the agent returns a fixed welcome string without calling the model. BOOKINGS state is process-global and shared by all conversations; booking codes depend on how many bookings exist so far. Guard quirks: nights is validated with isinstance int (JSON booleans would pass in Python, since bool is an int, though the tool schema types it int); a blank guest_name is only refused after city/room/nights/sold-out checks. Required env: one of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (either-or, so not listed in required_environment).
